title: Logging and auditing: CloudTrail and its equivalents

videos.script: Every change to a cloud account is a call to an API. {{calls}} CloudTrail writes one record for each call. Who made it, from where, when, and whether it was allowed. {{fields}} That record is often the only memory the account has. But a trail records less than people think. {{data}} Who changed a bucket's policy is recorded by default. Who downloaded the files while it was public is not, unless somebody chose it beforehand. {{trail}} You will build a trail in the lab, and watch moto keep its settings and write nothing. So the status says logging, and the bucket is empty. That is a lesson worth keeping. {{read}} Then you will read an afternoon of records with jq. A bucket goes public, two files leave, and a former contractor tries to switch the trail off. {{protect}} Last, you protect the trail from the people it records. {{end}}
